rounds.title: OTP input baseline
rounds.note: The SDK otp input (et-otp-input), first drawing, drawn by the mock from @ethlete/components/design/otp-input with the real markup and CSS: et-label with the required marker, the segment row, the invisible native input over it, et-form-support with hint and error; the brand theme, danger as the error theme. The field has no :focus or :hover CSS of its own: focus is the data-caret segment (a 1px border plus a 1px inset outline in primary, and a blinking 2px caret bar in an empty one), which the mock draws with focused. Fixtures are fictional: Verification code, 6 digits 482193, hint We sent it to +49 151 0000 0000., required with error Enter the code from the SMS.; a 4-digit masked PIN. Framed as a page with 16px padding at 320, 360 and 640. States: empty, partial, filled, hover, focus-empty, focus-partial, focus-filled, hint, required, invalid, invalid-partial, invalid-focus, disabled, disabled-filled, readonly, readonly-focus, pin-partial and pin-focus. Numbers (light / dark), from shot pixels at scale 2 at 360, brand mint, a: segment 44px outer (border-box, fixed in 00072d935), gap 8px, row 304px, digits 19.8px; empty and filled segment border (surface border) vs page 1.26 / 1.73, the only edge of a segment; caret segment edge and caret bar (primary) 1.33 / 13.50; required marker (brand primary) 1.33 / 13.50; invalid border (danger) 4.83 / 3.71; label (muted) 7.81 / 6.94; disabled digits 2.55 / 3.72 (opacity 0.4, exempt). Decided rules that arise: Q88 (focus in ink: the caret segment edge and the caret bar take ink, the invalid one the danger ink) and Q99a (a mint mark on light takes ink: the required marker light-dark(ink, primary)). Hover follows the text field (form-field-text-shell: the frame border to surface-interaction-hover, the error frame to ink, none when readonly or disabled), on the host since the host is the click target (otp.activate()). The filled segment edge in c is my proposal, not a decided rule (Q103). Findings for later, lib bugs apart: (L1) a 6-digit field needed 304px and never shrank; at 320 with 16px page padding it overflowed by 16px (drawn at 320). Now fixed: the segments shrink, 41.3px at 320, and the render at 640 is unchanged. (L2) a readonly field showed the focus caret segment and, when not full, the blinking caret bar, though nothing can be typed (readonly-focus). Now fixed: no caret when readonly. Design: (1) WCAG 1.4.11: the segment border 1.26 / 1.73 is the only edge of an empty segment, as with the checkbox box and the radio circle. Not drawn. (2) A filled segment looks like an empty one apart from its digit; c answers it. (3) The error border is the full danger primary, while the text field draws its error frame at 50 % danger; kept, it passes 3:1. (4) Hover (10.37 / 13.07) outshines the focus edge (5.48 / 13.50) in b and c, as it does on the text field. (5) The masked dot is a 19.8px bullet, about 5px wide. (6) The error marker 3.71 in dark, exempted as in checkbox r1. Later rounds, left out here: data-warning (no CSS of its own), a coloured field, alphanumeric codes, other lengths and segment sizes via the custom properties, RTL and the pop-in animation.

a.note: Today, the lib as is. On light the caret segment edge and the caret bar are mint 1.33 vs page (dark 13.50); the required marker 1.33; no hover; filled and empty segments share the 1.26 / 1.73 border. At 320 the row overflowed by 16px (L1, now fixed); readonly-focus showed the caret (L2, now fixed).

b.note: Pick. a plus Q88 and Q99a, decided rules only, and the text field hover. The caret segment edge and the caret bar in ink: light 5.48 vs page (was 1.33), dark the ink is the mint, 13.50 as today; the invalid one in the danger ink, 6.47 / 6.48 (was 4.83 / 3.71). The required marker light-dark(ink, primary), light 5.48 (was 1.33). Hover: every segment but the caret one to surface-interaction-hover, 10.37 / 13.07, the error ones to the danger ink; none when readonly or disabled. Empty and filled borders unchanged. Picked because it applies only decided rules plus the text field's own hover, so the otp input reads like the other fields.

c.note: b plus a filled segment edge in surface-interaction, 4.74 / 6.94 vs page (empty stays 1.26 / 1.73), so a typed digit's box shows and the next empty one reads as the gap to fill (Q103, my proposal, not a decided rule). The error state keeps the danger border on every segment; the caret segment keeps its ink edge.
